content.text:
The failures are real, but none of them come from these PRs' own code. Two separate things went wrong, and one is a real Turbodiff bug.

I couldn't open the feature pages (the browser pane isn't signed in to turbodiff.dev), and my read of the prod DB was blocked. So everything below comes from GitHub and the code, and I haven't seen the stored stage states. One mapping to know: `/factory/features/N` is delivery N, which is PR #196, #197 and #198.

## 1. Build: the factory's commits really did fail CI

| Feature | PR | Factory commit | CI on that commit | Your merge from main (20:07) | CI now |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | Add support for Opus 5.5 ([#196](https://github.com/Ngineer101/turbodiff/pull/196)) | `81815f1` | ❌ failed | `eb4045b` | ✅ passed |
| 3 | Dropdown not scrollable on mobile ([#197](https://github.com/Ngineer101/turbodiff/pull/197)) | `bafff91` | ❌ failed | `53d0193` | ✅ passed |
| 4 | Minor UX improvements ([#198](https://github.com/Ngineer101/turbodiff/pull/198)) | `12f4e74` | ❌ failed | `6d406d6` | ✅ passed |

All three branches were cut from a broken main. They failed the typecheck with the same error:

```
src/data/execution.ts:498:42 - error TS2339: Property 'costUsd' does not exist on type 'CliUsage'.
```

That was fixed by #195, merged at 20:06. You merged main into each branch a minute later, and that's why CI is green now. The PRs' own changes were fine the whole time.

What happened to the factory runs after the failure:
- CI failed, so each delivery went to repair.
- The repair agent pushed nothing, which makes sense because the error was outside the diff.
- The runs probably ended up parked or failed.

After that, `reconcileChangeDelivery` exits early when the run's status is `failed` ([delivery-lifecycle.ts:166](src/application/factory/delivery-lifecycle.ts:166)). So your green pushes won't restart review or verify by themselves. You'll need to hit Retry/Resume on each feature.

Your merge pushes should have recorded the new head and its green checks, so I'd expect Build to turn green. If it's still red, the new revision probably wasn't recorded. A DB read would tell us for sure.

## 2. Review: the #196 review is actually #197's review

This is a real Turbodiff bug. The review posted on #196 (Opus 5.5, which only touches migrations) describes the model-combobox change from #197, word for word. It even says so in its footer: *"Coverage incomplete: 0/3 reviewable files assessed. Missing: `db/migrations/0006_add_claude_opus_5_5.sql` …"*.

Here's the cause:
- `reviewSandbox()` gives every review in a repository the same sandbox, `review--ngineer101--turbodiff` ([sandbox.ts:38](src/integrations/agent-runtime/sandbox.ts:38)).
- The prompt and output files are named after the agent id only: `/workspace/review-${agent.id}.md` and `.json` ([review.ts:95](src/application/factory/stages/review.ts:95)).
- The reviews for #196 and #197 ran at the same time, 2 seconds apart, with the same reviewer agent. One overwrote the other's files, and both PRs got #197's result.
- On top of that, the cleanup deletes `/workspace/review-${stageRun.id}-*.json`, which never matches those file names, so old output files are never removed.

What this means for each feature:
- **Feature 2:** it's marked as a review with 0% coverage, so it's not a real review. Red is fair.
- **Feature 3:** its review is probably its own real one, but I can't tell which run's output it was.
- **Feature 4:** no review was ever posted on GitHub. I can't see from here whether the review stage failed or never ran.

## Suggested next steps
1. Fix the file collision by naming the prompt and output files after `stageRun.id` (plus the agent id), and fix the cleanup pattern to match. I can make this change with a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
2. Once that's in, resume all three deliveries so they get fresh reviews on the green heads.
3. To confirm the exact state of each Build and Review lamp, I need either your OK to run read-only queries on `turbodiff-prd` (`stage_runs` and `change_checks` for deliveries 2–4), or screenshots of the pages.

Want me to go ahead with the fix?

input.title: Track human pushes on factory PRs in review-only repos
input.tldr: Features 2–4 still show Build FAILED even though CI is green now: in the automatic_review profile, Turbodiff never records a new revision when someone pushes to a factory PR. This task makes the latest head and its checks show up on the feature page.
input.prompt:
In turbodiff (repo root), feature pages keep showing a stale Build lamp when a human pushes to a factory PR in a repository using the default `automatic_review` process profile (repository settings `{}`).

Evidence (prod, 2026-09-28): deliveries 2, 3, 4 (PRs Ngineer101/turbodiff#196, #197, #198). The factory commits failed CI on a broken main; the user then merged main into each branch (heads eb4045b, 53d0193, 6d406d6) and CI passed. But `app.change_revisions` still has only v1 per change (revisions 20, 21, 22 at the factory heads), and `app.change_checks` only holds the failed `CI (workflow 334405536, pull_request)` rows. So `src/client/lib/backend.ts` maps checks from the stale revision, and `stationsFor` in `src/client/pages/feature.tsx` shows Build FAILED.

Cause: in `src/application/webhooks/github.ts` `handlePullRequest`, `reconcile` only runs when `policy.verify` is on (it isn't for automatic_review), and a `synchronize` event returns early (`push reviews disabled`) before `syncGithubChangeRevision` when `reviewOnPush` is off. `handleWorkflowRun` records checks only for revisions found by `findChangesAtHead`, so the green run on the new head is dropped.

Goal: on `synchronize` for factory/automation changes, capture the new revision (`syncGithubChangeRevision`) even when push reviews are disabled, so later workflow_run webhooks attach checks to it. Don't trigger a review unless reviewOnPush is set. Decide how the Review lamp should show that the review covered an older revision. Ship a test that fails before the fix and passes after (see tests/unit and tests/integration). Follow AGENTS.md.

content.text:
The file collision is fixed and tested on `fix/review-file-collision`. Nothing is committed yet. The DB also showed that part of my earlier explanation was wrong, so here are the corrections.

## Corrections from the DB
- **No repair or verify ever ran.** Repository settings are `{}`, so this repo uses the `automatic_review` profile. Each delivery was marked `completed` as soon as its PR opened, and only the implement and review stages ran.
- **Turbodiff never saw your merge pushes.** Each change still has only its first revision, at the factory commit (`81815f1`, `bafff91`, `12f4e74`). The only stored checks are the failed `CI` runs from 18:42 and 19:24.
- **Why Build stays red:** with verify off and push reviews off, a `synchronize` event never records the new head as a revision. The green CI webhook for that head then has nothing to attach to, so it's dropped.

## Review, per feature
| Feature | Review stored | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 2 (#196) | `comment / inconclusive`, coverage incomplete | Not a real review: it's #197's result, caused by the collision |
| 3 (#197) | `approve / ready`, 0 findings | Its own real review |
| 4 (#198) | Stage failed (`agent_failed`) | The reviewer agent exited 1 partway through its analysis. Unrelated to the collision; it ran alone |

By the lamp code, features 2 and 3 should show Review GO. Only feature 4 should be red. If 2 and 3 really are red on the page, a screenshot would help me find out why.

## The fix
- **What changed:** a new helper, `reviewStageFiles(stageRunId)` in [review-workspace-policy.ts](src/integrations/agent-runtime/review-workspace-policy.ts), names the patch, prompt and output files after the stage run and the agent. [review.ts](src/application/factory/stages/review.ts) now uses it everywhere.
- **Why it collided:** the old files were named after the agent only, and all reviews in a repo share one sandbox. When #197's review started, it deleted and rewrote #196's files.
- **Cleanup:** the old cleanup pattern never matched those files. The new one matches every file a review stage writes.
- **Test:** added to `review-workspace.test.ts`. It passes with the fix. With the old agent-only names put back, it fails (`expected 4 to be 6`, meaning two reviews shared paths).
- **Checks:** `vp test` (325 tests) and `vp run check:types` pass. `vp check` still reports formatting issues in `agents.tsx` and `skills.tsx`, which were already there on main, so I left them alone.

The fix hasn't been run in prod. It'll count as proven once two PRs reviewed at the same time each get their own review.

## What's left
- **Stale Build lamp:** I opened a task chip, "Track human pushes on factory PRs in review-only repos", to record new heads on `synchronize` even when push reviews are off. That's what keeps 2–4 red now.
- **Feature 2** needs a fresh review, and **feature 4** a retry. With the collision fixed, a manual review on each (`createReviewRun`) would review the current green heads.
